---
title: "Further reading"
---

## Start here

| | |
|---|---|
| [R for Data Science (2e)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) | Wickham, Çetinkaya-Rundel & Grolemund. Free. The default next step |
| [The Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://epirhandbook.com/) | Task-oriented and health-specific. Excellent for lookups |
| [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/guide/) | Unusually good official docs |
| [gtsummary gallery](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/articles/gallery.html) | Copy the table closest to yours |

## Visualisation

- [ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis (3e)](https://ggplot2-book.org/): Wickham. Free.
- [Fundamentals of Data Visualization](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/): Wilke. On what to plot, not how.
- [Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction](https://socviz.co/): Healy. Social-science framing, R throughout.
- [R Graph Gallery](https://r-graph-gallery.com/): find a chart, take its code.

## Reproducibility

- Peng RD. [Reproducible research in computational science](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1213847). *Science* 2011.
- Baker M. [1,500 scientists lift the lid on reproducibility](https://doi.org/10.1038/533452a). *Nature* 2016.
- Ziemann M et al. [Gene name errors are widespread](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-1044-7). *Genome Biol* 2016.
- Wickham H. [Tidy data](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v059.i10). *JSS* 2014.
- [The Turing Way](https://the-turing-way.netlify.app/): the most complete free handbook on reproducible research.

## Statistics for medical education

- Norman G. [Likert scales, levels of measurement and the laws of statistics](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-010-9222-y). *Adv Health Sci Educ* 2010.
- Cook DA, Beckman TJ. [Validity and reliability for psychometric instruments](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amjmed.2005.10.036). *Am J Med* 2006.
- Sullivan GM, Artino AR. [Analyzing and interpreting data from Likert-type scales](https://doi.org/10.4300/JGME-5-4-18). *J Grad Med Educ* 2013.
- Altman DG, Doré CJ. [Randomisation and baseline comparisons in clinical trials](https://doi.org/10.1016/0140-6736(90)90709-5). *Lancet* 1990.

## Writing and publishing

- [Quarto manuscripts](https://quarto.org/docs/manuscripts/)
- [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/) + [Better BibTeX](https://retorque.re/zotero-better-bibtex/): reference management that plays well with Quarto
- [CSL style repository](https://www.zotero.org/styles): your journal's citation style
- [EQUATOR Network](https://www.equator-network.org/): reporting guidelines. Find yours before you write, not after.

## Generative AI in research

- [ICMJE Recommendations](https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/): the AI clause
- WHO. [Ethics and governance of AI for health: large multi-modal models](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240084759), 2024
- [Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023](https://www.meity.gov.in/data-protection-framework)
- [ICMR National Ethical Guidelines](https://ethics.ncdirindia.org/)
- [IndiaAI Mission](https://indiaai.gov.in/)

## Going further with R

- [Advanced R (2e)](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/): how R actually works
- [R Packages (2e)](https://r-pkgs.org/): when your functions outgrow a script
- [Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com/): the gentlest route into version control
- [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/): if your data have coordinates
- [Targets user manual](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/): pipelines that only re-run what changed

## Communities

- [R-Ladies](https://rladies.org/): chapters in several Indian cities
- [Posit Community](https://forum.posit.co/): friendlier than Stack Overflow for beginners
- [TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday): a new dataset every week, no stakes
